subject: Career
title: The Side Project Runway
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Side Project Runway.

hook.text: She didn't quit her accounting job to become a UX designer. She built a portfolio on nights and weekends.

buildup.text: The side project runway: build credibility in your new field while your current job pays the bills.

discovery.text: Freelance projects, volunteer work, and personal projects create a track record without financial risk.

twist.text: It takes longer — usually 6-18 months. But the transition is smoother and less financially terrifying.

climax.text: The goal: by the time you make the jump, you already have proof you can do the new work.

punchline.text: Build the bridge before you burn the old one.

quiz.question: What is the side project runway strategy?
options: Building credibility in a new field while your current job pays the bills
Only applying to jobs in the new field

details.summary: A side project runway is the practice of building skills, reputation, and income in a new field while still employed in your current one. It de-risks career transitions by providing proof of competence before you make the leap.
details.whyItMatters: Quitting first and figuring it out later leads to financial stress that compromises decision-making. A side project runway gives you evidence and confidence before the transition.
takeaways: Start your side project at least six to twelve months before a planned switch
Use it to build a portfolio and test market demand
Set clear milestones that signal when you are ready to transition

faq.question: How do you find time for a side project while working full-time?
faq.answer: Dedicate a consistent five to ten hours per week rather than sporadic bursts. Early mornings, weekends, or lunch breaks work. Consistency compounds; even two hours a day for six months produces a meaningful portfolio.

faq.question: Can an employer legally prevent you from having a side project?
faq.answer: Many employment contracts include non-compete or moonlighting clauses. Review your contract and company handbook carefully. Generally, side projects in a different industry using your own equipment and time are permissible, but always verify.
